Question: A triangle has vertices \((0, 0),\) \((1, 1),\) and \((6m, 0),\) and the line \(y = mx\) divides the triangle into two triangles of equal area. What is the sum of all possible values of \(m?\)
Solution:
Let \(O=(0,0)\), \(P=(1,1)\), and \(Q=(6m,0)\). We must have \(m\ne0\), since otherwise two vertices coincide.

The line \(y=mx\) passes through \(O\). To divide the triangle into two triangles, it must meet the interior of \(PQ\) at a point \(T\). The triangles \(OPT\) and \(OQT\) have the same altitude to line \(PQ\), so their areas are equal exactly when \(PT=TQ\). Thus \(T\) must be the midpoint of \(PQ\), with coordinates
\[
T=\left(\frac{1+6m}{2},\frac12\right).
\]
Substituting this point into \(y=mx\) gives
\[
\frac12=m\frac{1+6m}{2},
\]
so
\[
6m^2+m-1=(3m-1)(2m+1)=0.
\]
Therefore \(m=\frac13\) or \(m=-\frac12\). Both values give nondegenerate triangles, and in each case the line joins \(O\) to the opposite side's midpoint, so both are valid. Their sum is
\[
\frac13-\frac12=-\frac16.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{-\frac16}\), choice B.
